ideaStatement: Add in-loop completion enforcement to the csm skills that provably stop with work remaining (csm-build, csm-plan, csm-review, csm-orchestrate): each covered skill's own loop dispatches a fresh, independent, binding per-cycle evaluator that owns the continue/stop decision and journals a verdict receipt, backed by new csm-plan/2 and csm-build-state/2 revisions (typed supersession + terminal superseded), a strict migration of the existing corpus, and bundled in-loop fixes (conditional tmux bootstrap, strict acceptance signals, build input-gate alignment, review remediation-closure). Enforcement stays inside the loops — never in the Makefile or CI. The seven phases are delivered by ONE csm-plan invocation covering all phases (decision D10), not one plan per phase.

decisions.question: How is 'continue until complete' enforced given there is no opencode Stop hook and Makefile/CI are outside the loops?
decisions.answer: Enforcement lives INSIDE each covered skill's own loop (an independent per-cycle evaluator), never in the Makefile or CI; external gates are not the enforcement point.
decisions.rationale: The user's correction: checks/enforcement must be in the loops; Makefile/CI are outside them and cannot prevent a premature stop.

decisions.question: Which skills does the program cover?
decisions.answer: Only the skills with hard corpus evidence of the defect: csm-build, csm-plan, csm-review, csm-orchestrate.
decisions.rationale: Evidence-based scoping: build (6 stale trackers), plan (16 unclosed plans, 10 disjunctive signals), review (3/4 INCOMPLETE, no closure field), orchestrate (first-failure termination). Others unproven.

decisions.question: How is the in-loop guard made non-optional?
decisions.answer: An independent evaluator owns the continue/stop decision each cycle (generalizing csm-orchestrate's independent final review), rather than prose or an uncalled function.
decisions.rationale: An independent decision-maker removes the self-judged-stop defect (P7); draft-and-decide separation mirrors /goal and deep-research's challenger/judge.

decisions.question: What does the evaluator decide on, and how binding is it?
decisions.answer: It reads the skill's durable control (plan tasks/journal, build-state, review findings, orchestrate cursor/receipt) plus the goal and acceptance criteria, and returns continue | complete | blocked with evidence; the verdict is BINDING and journaled as a receipt.
decisions.rationale: A binding, evidence-based verdict with a receipt makes 'cannot end with work remaining' checkable inside the loop.

decisions.question: How to add a typed supersession link and a terminal superseded/abandoned state given immutable schemas?
decisions.answer: New csm-plan/2 and csm-build-state/2 revisions (typed supersession + terminal superseded); /1 stays frozen; dual-revision validators and consumers.
decisions.rationale: Registry immutability forbids in-place edits; the /1+/2 precedent already exists.

decisions.question: What is csm-orchestrate's behavior on a node failure?
decisions.answer: Keep fail-closed; the evaluator directs at most one bounded remainder phase; emit a typed resumable supersession pointer for the abandoned nodes/phases.
decisions.rationale: Preserves the fail-closed assurance entry (AGENTS.md) while removing the silent orphan of pending work.

decisions.question: How are the existing invalid records (27/60 plans, 12/23 build-state) treated?
decisions.answer: Strict enforcement on everything: the corpus is migrated to the /2 shape as a prerequisite phase, then no invalid record is accepted.
decisions.rationale: The user chose strict enforcement; that requires a migration phase before enforcement goes live.

decisions.question: Which ancillary in-loop fixes are bundled?
decisions.answer: Conditional tmux bootstrap (single-source boilerplate); strict acceptance-signal enforcement in csm-plan; align csm-build's input gate with its SKILL; csm-review remediation-closure linkage.
decisions.rationale: Each closes a specific finding inside the owning skill's loop; all are in-skill, not CI.

decisions.question: What is the evaluator, mechanically, in this opencode runtime?
decisions.answer: A fresh independent subagent dispatched per cycle (like deep-research's challenger/judge and orchestrate's independent final review), given the durable-control evidence and returning a journaled verdict.
decisions.rationale: There is no /goal or Stop hook in opencode; the repo already uses independent evaluator subagents for exactly this role.
traceability: design decision; scout U1/HBR; deep-research + orchestrate precedent

decisions.question: How are the seven phases consumed by planning — one plan per phase or one plan covering all?
decisions.answer: ONE csm-plan invocation covering ALL SEVEN phases (a single plan), not one plan per phase.
decisions.rationale: User instruction; avoids the successor/proliferation failure this program is fixing and mirrors the dynamic-worker-runtime precedent of one plan covering all phases.

researchSynthesis: SCOUT established: the tmux phrase is single-source (scripts/lib/boilerplate.mjs + sync-skill-boilerplate.mjs), so P1 is one edit + regen, not 8 hand edits; the canonical JSON records are ungated and 27/60 plans + 12/23 build-state records already fail strict validation, so strict enforcement (D7) requires a migration phase (P2); csm-plan/1 and csm-build-state/1 are digest-pinned/immutable, so supersession + a terminal superseded state need /2 revisions (D5); and there is NO in-repo opencode Stop hook — only pre-commit/check-suite/CI — so the user placed enforcement inside the skill loops via an independent per-cycle evaluator (D1/D3), generalizing the repo's existing evaluator-subagent patterns (csm-deep-research challenger/judge; csm-orchestrate independent final review; csm-autoresearch separate evaluator). Two findings ground the scope: finding #1 (csm-plan/csm-build) and finding #2 (suite-wide), the latter importing the former's 14 claims. Every decision is traced to a user answer and/or a cited file:line.

phases.title: Conditional tmux bootstrap
phases.goal: Stop any skill from ending the invocation before work runs when it is already inside an agent session.
deliverables: One edit to the single-source tmux boilerplate; regenerated SKILL.md + payload copies; drift check green.
scope: the 8 SKILL.md sites + bootstrap payload copies
outOfScope: Any change to non-tmux sections; any Makefile/CI change
constraints: Single-source edit only; regenerate payload in the same commit; keep the section present (check-suite MANIFEST.tmux stays true)
acceptanceHints: After regeneration, the bootstrap detaches/ends only for an interactive human CLI, never when already in an agent session (CSM_AGENT_SESSION_* present); check-suite stays green

phases.title: Evaluator contract, /2 schemas, corpus migration
phases.goal: Define the in-loop evaluator contract and give the durable records a valid /2 shape so strict enforcement is possible.
deliverables: csm-plan/2 and csm-build-state/2 registered schemas (typed supersession + terminal superseded); evaluator contract spec (inputs/outputs/receipt); migrated valid corpus (60 plans + 23 build-state records); dual-revision validators/consumers.
outOfScope: Behavior changes in the skill loops (later phases)
constraints: Registry immutability: new /2 ids only, /1 frozen
Migration must not silently drop pending tasks (map them to the /2 shape)
acceptanceHints: Both /2 schemas validate; the migrated corpus validates under /2 with 0 failures; /1 records still read

phases.title: csm-build in-loop evaluator + input-gate alignment
phases.goal: Make the csm-build loop unable to reach COMPLETE while tasks remain, via a binding per-cycle evaluator; align its input gate with its SKILL.
deliverables: Per-cycle evaluator dispatch + journaled receipt in the csm-build loop (cannot COMPLETE without a passing verdict); input gate treats ddd/norms as optional, matching the SKILL.
constraints: Evaluator is a fresh independent subagent
acceptanceHints: A run with pending tasks cannot reach COMPLETE without a passing evaluator receipt; input-gate tests pass for a plan without ddd/norms

phases.title: csm-plan in-loop evaluator + strict acceptance signals + supersession
phases.goal: Make csm-plan refuse to close a plan with pending tasks, reject disjunctive acceptance signals, and close a predecessor when it spawns a successor.
deliverables: Per-cycle evaluator in the csm-plan loop; acceptance-signal validation rejecting 'Either ... OR defer' (genuine deferrals become blocked tasks); supersession-on-creation that closes the predecessor.
outOfScope: Other skills' plan consumption behavior beyond supersession
constraints: Enforce inside the plan loop, not via external checks
Deferrals must carry a user decision
No proliferation without closing the predecessor
acceptanceHints: A disjunctive signal is refused; a successor plan closes its predecessor; evaluator blocks COMPLETE while tasks are pending

phases.title: csm-review in-loop evaluator + remediation-closure linkage
phases.goal: Make csm-review unable to save as VERIFIED with unresolved work, and link each finding to a closing action.
deliverables: Per-cycle evaluator in the csm-review loop; a remediation-closure/disposition link from findings to closing evidence.
constraints: Evaluator independent of the findings author
Do not claim VERIFIED with open findings
acceptanceHints: A review with unresolved findings cannot be saved VERIFIED; every finding carries a closure or an explicit disposition

phases.title: csm-orchestrate evaluator + bounded remainder + resumable supersession
phases.goal: Keep orchestrate fail-closed on a node failure while removing the silent orphan of pending work.
deliverables: Node/run-boundary evaluator; at most one bounded remainder phase; a typed resumable supersession pointer for abandoned nodes/phases.
acceptanceHints: A node failure stops the run closed AND records pending nodes + a resumable supersession pointer; at most one bounded remainder phase runs

phases.title: Integration acceptance: no covered loop can end with work remaining
phases.goal: Prove end-to-end that the four covered skills cannot terminate with work remaining under strict enforcement.
deliverables: An acceptance suite + recorded evidence: each skill's loop refuses COMPLETE/SAVED with pending work absent a passing evaluator receipt; strict validation of all canonical records at 0 failures.
outOfScope: New features beyond the four skills
constraints: Failure of any covered loop is a release blocker
acceptanceHints: All four loops demonstrably refuse premature termination; the full canonical corpus validates under strict /2 rules
